'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022–2023 Peruvian political protests]]
**[[Juliaca massacre]]
***At least 18 people are killed and over 100 others are injured when the [[Peruvian National Police]] fire upon [[2022–2023 Peruvian political protests|demonstrations]] in [[Juliaca]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/least-nine-dead-anti-government-protests-near-peru-airport-2023-01-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Maluku earthquake]]
**One person is killed and eight others are injured after a [[moment magnitude scale|magnitude]] 7.6–7.9 earthquake hits off the coast of eastern [[Indonesia]], causing damage to buildings, and shaking buildings as far away as [[Darwin, Northern Territory|Darwin]], [[Australia]]. [https://www.malukuterkini.com/2023/01/10/catat-ini-data-kerusakan-akibat-gempa-m-79-di-tanimbar/ (Maluku Terkini)]
*Two people are killed in a [[plane crash]] near the town of [[Karataika]], [[Nenets Autonomous Okrug]], in [[Russia]]'s far north. A total of twelve people were on board the plane. [https://www.rferl.org/a/plane-crash-russia-far-north/32215900.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
***[[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[China]] reopens its borders for unrestricted travel, marking the repeal of the country's last [[Zero-COVID]] policy. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/travel/news/china-s-open-borders-mark-covid-zero-end-spark-homecoming-rush/ar-AA165vAN?OCID=ansmsnnews11 (Bloomberg)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[8 January Brasília attacks|2023 Brazilian Congress attack]]
**Around 1,200 supporters of former [[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] are arrested following yesterday's riots in [[Brasília]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2023/01/09/world/brazil-congress-riots-bolsonaro (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Armenia–Russia relations]], [[2022–2023 blockade of the Republic of Artsakh]]
**Protests break out in the city of [[Gyumri]] in [[Armenia]] against the [[Russian 102nd Military Base|Russian military presence in the country]] and the Russian peacekeepers' inaction in ending the Lachin corridor blockade. Dozens of protesters are arrested by police after they attempted to reach the Russian military base near the city to blockade it. [https://oc-media.org/dozens-arrested-at-russian-military-base-protest-in-gyumri/ (OC Media)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Gabonese President]] [[Ali Bongo Ondimba]] names [[Alain Claude Bilie By Nze]] as the new prime minister and head of government, replacing [[Rose Christiane Raponda]]. [https://english.news.cn/20230110/e577cb95b8bc4adb9fe0ee01157e8aa0/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[British space programme]]
**[[Virgin Orbit]]'s [[LauncherOne]] fails to reach the [[Low Earth orbit]] with a payload of several [[CubeSat|small satellites]] after the rocket suffered a [[Two-stage-to-orbit|second-stage]] engine anomaly on its ascent to space, resulting in the loss of the payload. The mission, which launched from [[Spaceport Cornwall]] in [[South West England]], would have been the first rocket launched from [[United Kingdom]] territory. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/historic-uk-rocket-mission-ends-in-failure-scientists-report-anomaly-101673314651211.html (AFP via ''Hindustan Times'')]
*An [[Solar_flare#Classification|X1.9-class]] [[solar flare]] erupts from an active [[sunspot]] while facing [[Earth]] causing temporary [[radio]] blackouts in parts of [[South America]], according to the [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]]. The source is "hyperactive sunspot AR3184", which also caused a X1.2-class solar flare on January 5. [https://www.space.com/huge-solar-flare-eruption-hyperactive-sunspot (Space.com)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 College Football Playoff National Championship]]
**In [[American football]], the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] repeat as national champions, defeating the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]] in a 65–7 blowout. [https://www.npr.org/2023/01/09/1147979385/georgia-bulldogs-tcu-horned-frogs-college-football-championship (NPR)]
*Aftermath of the [[2021 NWSL abuse scandal]]
**The [[National Women's Soccer League]] of the United States bans former coaches [[Richie Burke]] of [[Washington Spirit]], [[Rory Dames]] of [[Chicago Red Stars]], [[Christy Holly]] of [[Racing Louisville FC|Racing Louisville]], and [[Paul Riley (footballer)|Paul Riley]] of [[North Carolina Courage]] for life following an investigation on allegations of abuse throughout the [[2021 National Women's Soccer League season|2021 season]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2023/01/09/nwsl-punishment-misconduct/ (''The Washington Post'')]
